nodes.label: Bit-vector classifier (LPM + port classes + bitmap AND)
nodes.norm_label: bit-vector classifier (lpm + port classes + bitmap and)
nodes.rationale: First-match rule selection as 16 u64 ANDs of source/destination LPM bitmaps and a service bitmap, with de Bruijn first_set_bit; LPM folding done by the Compiler because LPM returns only the longest prefix; ~6 lookups per new Flow keeps the verifier budget feasible (risk R1).

nodes.label: Own conntrack state machine (SYN map separation)
nodes.norm_label: own conntrack state machine (syn map separation)
nodes.rationale: Half-open Flows live in a small LRU ct_syn map so a SYN flood evicts only half-open entries; promotion to ct_main happens on the first reply, not the SYN; lazy timeouts avoid per-packet timer work.

nodes.label: struct ct_entry (96 B conntrack entry)
nodes.rationale: Carries policy_gen (gen_seq that accepted the Flow, ADR-0004) and a peer key so policy-change re-classification and deletion of both directions work without a mass sweep; 96 B matches ADR-0006 memory estimate; layout is a contract enforced by _Static_assert.

nodes.label: Drop reason enum (0..12, stable wire values)
nodes.norm_label: drop reason enum (0..12, stable wire values)
nodes.rationale: Enum mirrored in Go in one generated file; adding a reason is a schema-of-record change (both sides, one PR).

nodes.label: Per-CPU token bucket event rate limiting
nodes.norm_label: per-cpu token bucket event rate limiting
nodes.rationale: R-026.1: 1000 tokens/s per CPU with 4x burst protects the ring buffer from event floods; lost events counted via counters_misc[events_lost]; FLOW_END emitted only from the Go sweeper because the kernel cannot know a packet is the last.

nodes.label: struct flow_event (80 B ring buffer record)
nodes.norm_label: struct flow_event (80 b ring buffer record)
nodes.rationale: Sized to fit ~100k records in the 8 MiB ring buffer; carries policy_gen so events name the Policy that matched.

nodes.label: Generation swap protocol (two-generation maps)
nodes.rationale: Atomic apply: build a fresh generation in the inactive gen_maps slot, self-check, flip active_gen with one 4-byte Map.Update; failure leaves provably intact previous state; old generation retained for instant rollback; CT entries not swept — staleness is tested by policy_gen, not rule_idx, because a reorder would make the same index resolve to a different Policy.

nodes.label: NAT design: DNAT in TC ingress, SNAT in TC egress
nodes.norm_label: nat design: dnat in tc ingress, snat in tc egress
nodes.rationale: DNAT target pre-matched in XDP and carried in sb_meta so TC ingress only rewrites; SNAT port picked by hash + linear probe with BPF_NOEXIST into snat_rev; reverse SNAT restores original destination before CT lookup.

nodes.label: struct sb_meta (32-byte XDP→TC context handoff)
nodes.rationale: Carries the DNAT target and classification results so the TC programs never re-look-up dnat_candidates; sized 32 B because data_meta requires a multiple of 4.

nodes.label: Milestones M0–M5 with detailed-design-before-code rule
nodes.rationale: Every code-producing WBS branch is preceded by a detailed-design document written in an earlier milestone (data plane at M0, control plane at M1, REST API at M5); critical path M0 → M2 → M4 → M5.

nodes.label: Monorepo songbird-fw (ADR-0011)
nodes.rationale: One PR can touch requirement, ADR, schema, code and test together; one CI; one issue tracker; traceability matrix trivial to generate; history preserved via git subtree add.

nodes.label: MVP 0.1 scope (41 requirements: 39 Must, 2 Should)
nodes.rationale: A stateless firewall proves nothing, so R-045.x (statefulness) is in; Web UI, auth, IPv6, DHCP/DNS/NTP deferred because they are independent of the risky parts or are rework on an unproven model; performance targets measured in 0.1, met in 1.0.

nodes.label: Release roadmap 0.1 → 1.0
nodes.rationale: Every release is a usable firewall, not a pile of components; internal order design → detailed design → tests → code → verification; 0.1 proves the two riskiest bets (eBPF classifier + own conntrack, and YAML→validate→compile→atomic apply) — everything not serving those proofs is deferred, including Must requirements.

nodes.label: Risk register R1–R10
nodes.rationale: Top risks: eBPF verifier rejecting the classifier/conntrack (R1, mitigated by small tail-called programs and PROG_TEST_RUN) and bus factor 2 (R2, mitigated by review-everything and scope lever rather than quality lever).

nodes.label: Python validator dependencies (jsonschema, pyyaml)
nodes.rationale: Dependencies of validate.py, the Python reference validator later ported to Go as 'songbird validate' (R-052).

nodes.label: Suites S1–S8 required for release 0.1
nodes.rationale: S3 fuzz and S5 PMTUD scheduled early because they are the most likely to surface design bugs.

nodes.label: Test-ID convention <L1|L2|L3|L4>-<AREA>-<NNN>
nodes.rationale: IDs never reused; a removed test keeps its ID as withdrawn; linkage via '// Verifies: R-…' annotations so the matrix can be generated.

nodes.label: Test levels L1–L6 (unit/integration/system/perf/inspection/analysis)
nodes.rationale: No mocks in L2 because namespaces, veth and the real kernel stack are the point; tests precede code in the same PR; flaky tests are release blockers.

nodes.label: Generated traceability matrix
nodes.rationale: Generated, never hand-edited; enforcement ramps: red fails the pipeline from M1, uncovered Must requirements become blocking only from M5 so the M1 'mostly uncovered' state is not contradictory; a Must requirement without a test is a release blocker for 1.0.

nodes.label: ADR-0002: XDP decides, kernel forwards, TC rewrites
nodes.norm_label: adr-0002: xdp decides, kernel forwards, tc rewrites
nodes.rationale: XDP_REDIRECT bypasses TC egress, and PPPoE/VLAN lack native XDP; splitting policy (XDP) from NAT (TC) works on all netdevices while drops stay at XDP speed.

nodes.label: ADR-0007: Reference platform
nodes.rationale: Performance requirements are meaningless without a fixed reference (C-003); driver-dependent features (native XDP, XDP metadata, TCX) must be verified on known hardware.

nodes.label: ADR-0010: DNAT as a Policy section, pre-translation match
nodes.norm_label: adr-0010: dnat as a policy section, pre-translation match
nodes.rationale: Schema precedence over domain model: nat.type dnat reuses Address/Service objects, drops the VirtualIP kind and the VIP classifier dimension, and matches before translation (nftables prerouting semantics).

nodes.label: ADR-0013: Kernel >= 6.6, TCX, XDP native with generic fallback
nodes.norm_label: adr-0013: kernel >= 6.6, tcx, xdp native with generic fallback
nodes.rationale: TCX (kernel 6.6) gives link-managed ordered TC attach fitting the generation-swap design; one attach path avoids a double test matrix; Debian 13 (6.12) satisfies the floor.

nodes.label: ADR-0014: DHCP/DNS engines (open)
nodes.rationale: Decision not taken: in-process Go libraries (one binary, natural Prepare/Commit) vs external daemons (mature DNSSEC, process isolation) vs hybrid; criteria recorded pending a spike before M3.

nodes.label: ADR-0015: Go for the Control Plane
nodes.norm_label: adr-0015: go for the control plane
nodes.rationale: C-004 demands one static binary on an immutable OS; Go offers the best batteries for API/UI/Git/DNS/DHCP orchestration while the fast path stays in eBPF C.

nodes.label: ADR-0016: cilium/ebpf + bpf2go
nodes.rationale: Pure Go (no CGo, keeps static binary), CO-RE, and bpf2go-generated bindings make kernel/userspace struct layout a compile-time contract instead of a convention.

nodes.label: ADR-0003: Own conntrack in BPF maps
nodes.norm_label: adr-0003: own conntrack in bpf maps
nodes.rationale: Avoids grey-area nf_conntrack dependency under C-001, gives predictable performance/memory and full flow observability, at the cost of no ALGs.

nodes.label: ADR-0004: Re-classify active flows on policy change
nodes.norm_label: adr-0004: re-classify active flows on policy change
nodes.rationale: R-054 requires blocked flows to die at next packet; storing policy_gen per CT entry terminates newly-forbidden flows without flushing still-permitted ones.

nodes.label: ADR-0006: Data Plane capacity limits
nodes.rationale: eBPF maps and the bitmap classifier have fixed sizes set at creation, so limits (1024 policies/ruleset, 1M flows, 4096+ policies) must be pre-decided and validated before Apply.

nodes.label: ADR-0001: YAML in Git as single source of truth
nodes.norm_label: adr-0001: yaml in git as single source of truth
nodes.rationale: One store avoids drift between UI/CLI/GitOps; Git gives diff/review/history/revert for free; runtime state stays ephemeral and is rebuilt from HEAD.

nodes.label: ADR-0008: Schema versioning, migration and rollback
nodes.norm_label: adr-0008: schema versioning, migration and rollback
nodes.rationale: A/B updates plus a persistent Git config create forward/backward compatibility problems; in-place migration with pre-schema tag and fallback commit preserves R-019 without rewriting history or a second source of truth.

nodes.label: ADR-0009: Secrets encryption key protection
nodes.rationale: Secrets travel with the Git repo (push/export/HA) so disk encryption alone fails; app-level AEAD with a master key outside the repo, TPM-sealed when available, protects the journey while keeping unattended boot.

nodes.label: ADR-0012: Canonical YAML serialisation and file layout
nodes.norm_label: adr-0012: canonical yaml serialisation and file layout
nodes.rationale: The YAML text is the review surface; one canonical form (quoted strings, one object per file) makes diffs stable and exports byte-reproducible while input stays unconstrained.

nodes.label: ADR-0017: Hadron (Kairos) as appliance OS
nodes.rationale: R-019 A/B updates and C-002 immutability are properties of the Kairos/Hadron base rather than code to build; acceptance gated on kernel>=6.6, bpffs, TPM and a real A/B cycle.

nodes.label: ADR-0018: CRD-style configuration objects
nodes.rationale: Kubernetes resource shape (apiVersion/kind/metadata/spec) gives free JSON-Schema editor tooling, per-object metadata, kind dispatch, and a GitOps mental model the team already thinks in.
